note: Gate spec for the shared paste-enforcement Stop hook (hooks/paste-gate.py in the
agent-skills repo, installed as ~/.claude/hooks/paste-gate.py). The engine, the
failure it guards against and the detection rules are documented there.
`threads.py sync` is deliberately NOT gated even though the "status-only" doc path
pastes its output too: the opener also runs `sync` as silent,
intentionally-unshown prep (identical command text), so gating it would false-block
every opener turn demanding a redundant paste of that silent prep call. `todo` has no
such double-duty — it's only ever the user-facing status answer — so it's safe.

Re-send your message starting with the FULL `present` output pasted verbatim: the MR title line, the overview table, and (if there is one) the first open topic's blockquoted comment. Do not summarise it or lead with your own research prose.

note: The inverse of the diff-view gate: that gate only fires once diff-view.sh has RUN,
so skipping the script entirely — asking for the ACK straight out of prose — used to
pass unseen. SKILL.md states it as an absolute: never ask for the ACK without the
diff actually shown. The phrase is the script's own closing line, so a legitimate
message containing it has necessarily pasted diff-view's output (and the gate above
then checks the whole block); a message containing it with no run behind it can only
have written it out itself.
Anchored to a line start (with markdown/blockquote prefixes allowed) so that merely
TALKING about the phrase mid-sentence — editing this skill, quoting SKILL.md — is not
a hit; only presenting it as the ask is.
There is deliberately NO equivalent rule for change-preview's 'Agreed?': the
non-trivial branch ends with a plain discussion question, which can legitimately be
phrased that way, so it would block correct turns.
